question: What canonical skill permission and trust model should OpenClaw adopt for skills, and which parts belong in core, ClawHub, plugins, or installer policy?
rationale: The item crosses public schema design, user consent, signing/attestation semantics, runtime enforcement, and ClawHub trust signals, so automation cannot safely choose the security boundary.

options.title: Design a versioned core manifest contract
options.body: Define a narrow v0 manifest and grant model in core with ClawHub and plugin hooks consuming the same schema.

options.title: Limit this issue to inspect-only audit metadata
options.body: Ship only non-enforcing manifest parsing and audit display first, leaving grants, signing, and attestation to separate follow-up issues.

options.title: Move trust policy outside core
options.body: Route most permission analysis to ClawHub/plugins while keeping this issue open only for missing core API seams those tools require.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned core manifest contract
recommendation.body: Define a narrow v0 manifest and grant model in core with ClawHub and plugin hooks consuming the same schema.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history and discussion connect this owner to the central skills, plugin trust, and security review surfaces.
